Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. DVDs of the proceedings are available for purchase in the City
Clerk's Office. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818) 937-8100. Public
comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is discussed. If you have
any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance, please contact the City Clerk
at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

 5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine attended the City tree lighting event at Glendale City Hall and thanked
  the Community Services & Parks department for organizing the program. She acknowledged
  Stephen Meek for MCing the event. Councilmember Devine, together with the other council
  members, attended the Montrose Christmas Parade and congratulated the organizers on a
  successful event. Devine also attended the Glendale Association of Realtors to witness the
  installation of officers and congratulated Liza Boubari who was named “Citizen of the Year.”
  Devine was proud to participate in the Zonta Burbank chapter event called “Sixteen Days of
  Activism Against Gender Based Violence.”

  Councilmember Asatryan attended a private showing of the installation “Shelter” by the She
  Loves Collective, together with some of her colleagues. She acknowledged that this event
  was inspired by community member, Malcolm Johnson, who was sitting in the audience and
  thanked him for bringing forth an idea of creating a space for healing for the Armenian
  American community who have lost their loved ones in the war. Asatryan also acknowledged
  the Library and Arts staff who took on that request that came from oral communication and
  collaborated with local artists to create this wonderful space. The installation is located at 215
  North Orange Street and is going to run through January 29th, Wednesdays through Fridays
  6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. and Saturdays and Sundays from 12:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.. Asatryan
  stated it was one of the most moving installations she has ever attended. She thanked
  everyone who made the installation possible and encouraged the public to attend. Asatryan
  attended the Armenian Trade Show that had roughly 50 businesses visiting from Armenia.
  About 1000 people attended the trade show over the weekend at the Glendale Civic Plaza.
  This coming Friday, at the Glendale Central Library from 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m., the California
  Armenian Legislative Caucus Foundation is hosting an SPA Program and Services. She
  encouraged all small business owners to attend to learn about SPA programs and resources,
  economic aid programs and accessing grants and loans. For questions, the public can call
  916.396.9738.

  Councilmember Najarian asked staff to provide a report on LADWP’s scattergood energy
  plan. He also mentioned that the LA County Board of Supervisors directed the LA County
  Public Works to identify sensitive locations where flooding could occur due to climate change,
  however, none of the identified locations were in Glendale. He stated that Glendale is also
  vulnerable and has experienced devastating floods like the one in 1934 and he wants to make
  sure that if the county is providing funding, Glendale also receives some of this funding to
  improve the walls or channels in Glendale’s flood-prone areas.

  Mayor Pro Tem Brotman also attended the private showing of the installation “Shelter” by the
  She Loves Collective. He also acknowledged Malcolm Johnson’s contribution as well as the
  Glendale Arts and Culture and the She Loves Collective artists, including Mari Mansourian
  who is a City employee, for their part in making this impressive exhibit happen in less than two
  months. He attended the Electric Vehicle Test Drive event on Saturday and stated that there
  were 214 people who came to test-drive electric vehicles and there were 365 drives in 13
  different vehicles. Brotman asked staff to also look into including electric bikes in future
  events. Asatryan seconded. Lastly, he indicated that the November 6 election count has been
  completed and congratulated US Rep. Adam Schiff, Assembly Member Laura Friedman, and
  Assembly Member Wendy Carrillo, who is now representing the section of Glendale located
  south of the134. Brotman hopes that Assemblymember Carrillo would visit Glendale City Hall
  and meet with council. Councilmember Brotman also congratulated the newly-elected
  councilmembers for the City of Burbank – Nikki Perez, Tamala Takahasi and Zizette Mullins.
  Brotman stated that he looks forward to collaborating with the City of Burbank on issues of

  3
   common interest, including housing, mobility, energy and water.

  City Manager Roubik Golanian had announcements for two community meetings: 1) As
  Council directed staff to close the Scholl Canyon landfill by December of 2025, the next step in
  the process is to conduct a community meeting to get feedback on the future of the landfill
  once it is closed. This meeting will take place on December 7th from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m. at
  Jewel Bridge Clubhouse at Glenoaks Park. 2) Golanian invited the public to attend the
  Glenoaks Wildfire Awareness and Fire Plan on December 14th at Glenoaks Elementary
